items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: He brought Nat, he brought Nat King Cole around to my home... So they would rehearse the band, and then oh, we'd have marvelous sessions

ctx.x: Well, I'm glad you're glad. Well, you have such a distinctive voice, it's a wonderful style, that nobody has ever sounded like you.

Well, I'm glad of that too. I'm glad of that too. But you know, of course I suppose I had the same experience that Nat King Cole had, and there are a few other musicians too that has had the same experience. When I went to work, for instance my very first job here was at the
Dunbar Hotel. Did we talk about this the other day? I don't know.

items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I'm sure Carlos Gastell didn't have to have Nellie Lutcher at that time, because he had Nat Cole and all these other people that I just mentioned

ctx.x: He took good care of his artists.

Because he would see to it that you got recognition. That's one thing you did get, you know. And he didn't go for any peanuts, you know, he didn't go for that. So I was very fortunate, and I was very grateful to Mr. Dexter, because I'm sure Carlos Gastell didn't have to have Nellie Lutcher at that time, because he had Nat Cole and all these other people that I just mentioned, so he surely didn't need Nellie Lutcher.
I want to say something now, that recently there has been an article that Mrs. Nat King Cole wrote. It was the biography of Nat King Cole. Did you read that?
